summary: Updates the IANA considerations for the Layer Two Tunneling Protocol, describing how values for its registries should be assigned. It is a Best Current Practice and invites suggestions for improvement.

eli5.summary: Whenever a new L2TP feature needs a number, someone has to hand it out fairly. This note updates the rules for who gets which number and how.

subtitle: How to allocate numbers for L2TP protocol extensions

tldr.problem: The original L2TP registry rules were inconsistent: some registries required strict IETF consensus when the protocol had room for thousands of values, while vendors needed assigned numbers to start shipping working code.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3438 updates the IANA registry policies to relax some requirements from IETF Consensus to Expert Review, allowing qualified extensions to get values faster without formal standards documents.
tldr.outcome: The change lets the protocol evolve while preventing conflicts. It is a Best Current Practice guide for implementing L2TP.

today: RFC 3438 remains a Best Current Practice and continues to govern L2TP registry assignments.

sections.title: Problem and Solution
sections.content:
L2TP defines several registries of magic numbers used by the protocol. The initial rules required IETF Consensus for some of these registries, but the ranges were large (0 to 65,535), only a few values had been used, and there was no realistic risk of running out. This made it hard for vendors to deploy new features while documents were still in standardization.

RFC 3438 updates the assignment criteria: most registries now use Expert Review instead of IETF Consensus, allowing faster value assignment while still preventing mistakes.
sections.eli5: L2TP has a lot of room for new feature numbers. The old rules made vendors wait a long time for a number. The new rules let experts hand them out faster.

sections.title: Registry Updates
sections.content: Four registries are affected: Control Message Attribute Value Pairs, Message Type AVP Values, Result Code AVP Values, and General Error Codes. In one case, the criteria moved from First Come First Served to Expert Review to be more strict. In most cases, criteria moved from IETF Consensus to Expert Review to be more relaxed. The Designated Expert must check that the value is in an active document and that vendors are implementing it, not just planning to.
sections.eli5: Some lists of feature numbers changed their rules: mostly to let experts decide faster, in one case to be more careful.

sections.title: Intent and Practice
sections.content: The change was motivated by real cases in which vendors released products with their own temporary feature numbers while waiting for IETF documents to finish. This resulted in products that had to support both the vendor number and the official number forever. Expert Review gives enough oversight to prevent errors but allows faster value assignment for real working code.
sections.eli5: Vendors sometimes had to pick their own numbers before IETF approval. This update lets them get official numbers faster so they don't have to do that.
